subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Rahul speaks easily in front of a small group, but he seems ________ before a large audience.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"ill at ease"** means feeling uncomfortable or worried in a particular situation. (असहज)

 
 
• **Example:** She always felt **ill at ease** in social gatherings.
 
 
 
• **"ill at ease"** refers to a state of discomfort or unease, often in social situations or unfamiliar environments. (असहज)
 
 
• **Example:** Rahul was **ill at ease** before the large audience, despite his confidence in smaller groups.
 
 

Therefore, the most appropriate idiom is** 'malfunctioned.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Think ill of** (बुरा सोचना): To have a bad opinion about someone or something.

 
 
• **Example:** She tends to** think ill **of people who disagree with her.
 
 
 
• **Man of ill repute** (बदनाम व्यक्ति): A man known for having a bad reputation.
 
 
• **Example:** He was considered a** man of ill** repute in the town due to his shady business dealings.
 
 
 
• **Ill-disposed to** (असहमत): Not friendly or sympathetic towards.
 
 
• **Example:** She was** ill-disposed to** the idea of moving to a new city.
